name: Sikule
catalog_quote: In Sichule, like in Simalur, the accent generally lies on the final syllable, whereas Nias has penultimate accent. When suffixes are added to a stem the accent usually moves to the newly created final syllable, i.e. lies on the (final) suffix. When the 2nd person pl. possessive suffix, a syllabic -m, is added to a noun, the accent falls on this syllabic nasal. (Köhler 1955)

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Both deciding texts are confirmed verbatim in copies we hold, and they agree on word-final accent that shifts onto suffixes (word domain, final = final stress), so the direction of the classification is not in doubt and nothing found contradicts it. But the evidence is entirely second-hand (a 2015 database paraphrase and a one-line handbook citation of a 1955 German grammar sketch we do not hold), and the paraphrase itself hedges ('generally lies on the final syllable', 'usually moves'), which leaves the counts as exceptionless (the strict set) flag unverified. No later phonological or instrumental work on Sikule exists per Glottolog (2 desc refs, both Kähler 1955), Crossref, archive.org and the two open Sigulai papers downloaded now (both silent on stress). Status thin; action: obtain Kähler 1955 (library print) and re-read the accent section to confirm or relax 'strict' and to replace the empty quote/cite/loc with a primary
audit.second_reader_evidence: Quote finding re-verified independently. (1) K&H 'Suprasegmental phonology': the sentence '..as well as Sumatra, e.g. Sikule (Kähler 1955), Gayo (Eades 2005:31), Besemah (McDonnell 2014), Lampung (Walker 1975) but exceptions abound' is at line 147 of and extracted text of the sibling PDF returns it (PDF page 3, as cited). In context 'exceptions abound' refers to the areal distribution (next sentence: Nias and Mentawai are penultimate), not to Sikule-internal lexical exceptions, so it does not bear on the strict flag. (2) StressTyp2 SQL dump
